quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Points on your driving record:

options.text: Are nothing to worry about.
Are good to have.
Help you get a driving job.
Are bad to have on your record.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are bad to have on your record.
questions.explanation: When you get a traffic ticket while driving, points are added to your record. Too many points can cause you to lose your license.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signals whenever you move left or right. Signal when changing lanes, entering traffic from a parking space, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on hazard lights and hold on tight.
Steer firmly, slow down, and drive to a safe area to stop.
Press hard on the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, and drive to a safe area to stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need more force to steer. Slow down and pull off the road safely to stop.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go, but first check that pedestrians and other traffic have cleared the intersection.

questions.question: An intermediate license has these restrictions:

options.text: The driver must wear a seat belt.
All passengers must wear seat belts.
No driving between 1:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Intermediate license holders cannot drive alone from 1:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. except for school or work. The driver and all passengers must wear seat belts.

questions.question: If another car might hit you, you should:

options.text: Use your horn.
Wave your arms.
Turn on emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. This is especially important if another vehicle is about to hit you.

questions.question: You can reduce hydroplaning by:

options.text: Driving through shallow water.
Driving faster.
Driving slower.
Driving through deep water.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the road with no one inside it.
When it approaches you, even if lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop while the red lights flash or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Signal your intention to turn.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.
Call the police on your cell phone to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call the police on your cell phone to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you and signal your intention. Look for other drivers moving into the same lane. Never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.
Right turns are not allowed.
Left turns are allowed.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: This is a law sign. It means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: Your car hits a parked vehicle and you cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done enough.
You must wait for police to arrive.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.
You can leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass.
Do not enter.
No turn on red.
Keep right.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you a divided highway is coming. The road will split into two separate one-way roads. Stay on the right side.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
Pedestrians may be in the area.
A reduced speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: A reduced speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: School zones have lower speed limits during certain times. An "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at passengers while having a conversation during driving.
Only watches the car in front of them.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for items in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road and checking your mirrors regularly. These safe habits help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: When you turn right, where should your car be?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you start to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move as far to the right side of the road as you can. Do not cut across other lanes when turning.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or when they do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers on the road to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What colors are highway exit signs?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.explanation: Signs that give you directions are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down to safely handle these curves.

questions.question: How can you tell others you want to be an organ donor?

options.text: Fill out the organ donor section on the back of your license.
Tell your family about your decision.
Have two witnesses sign the back of your license.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To register as an organ donor, sign up online or in person when you apply for or renew your license. Fill out the back of your license completely and tell your family about your choice.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Protecting yourself from bad drivers by passing them in traffic.
Driving very close behind the vehicle in front of you.
Changing lanes quickly and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes caused by aggressive, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It increases your risk of crashing.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It reduces alcohol's effects on your driving.
It does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases your risk of crashing.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can harm your brain function and impair your driving. Mixing alcohol with other drugs greatly increases your crash risk.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction. You can only cross them to turn left or pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter riders when it is safe.

questions.question: After an accident where someone is injured, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them wrong can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: What happens to your field of vision when you speed up?

options.text: It gets wider.
It gets narrower.
It makes it easier to see crossing traffic.
It stays the same.

questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As speed increases and vision narrows, you must watch more carefully for hazards.
